title: A release sha now carries two CI runs and install_ci_state reads only one of them
body:
Since the macOS legs moved to release tags (issue 0046), a release commit carries TWO runs of `tests.yml`: the branch push, whose macOS legs are skipped, and the tag push, which runs them. `install_ci_state` asks `gh run list --commit <sha> --workflow tests.yml --limit 1` (`opt/utilz/lib/install.sh:674`), so it reads whichever run is newest, and GitHub documents no order between the branch and the tag push events of one `git push`.

WHAT READS IT: `tools/ci-state` is the release core's `ci.query`, and the core asks it at step 11, after it has pushed the tag. So a cut can record `green` on the strength of the Ubuntu-only run while the macOS run that carries the bash 3.2 coverage was red, or record a verdict from the tag run while the branch run was the red one. `utilz install` and `upgrade` record the same answer in the manifest, which is how a publish says what CI thought of the commit it published.

IT CANNOT BE FIXED BY PICKING THE RIGHT RUN. Whichever run is "the" run is a guess about an order GitHub does not promise, and the next workflow change moves it again.

THE FIX: the one function that asks CI reads EVERY run on the commit and answers with the worst, which is the rule `tools/ci-state` already states in its own header, that every conclusion which is not success is failed. Precedence, worst first: a row that cannot be read, then a conclusion that is not success, then a run still going, then a completed run with no conclusion, then success. The detail names the deciding run, and how many runs were read when there was more than one. There is still exactly one function asking CI, which is the property issue 0016 established.

TESTS, in `install_lib.bats`: two runs of which one failed reads failure; two of which one is still going reads pending; two green read success. AND THE REQUEST ITSELF IS ASSERTED, because no parse test can see a `--limit` of 1: the stub prints what it is told whatever it was asked, so a test that only feeds it two rows would pass against the unfixed function.
